claims.claim: Rather than increasing collaboration, open architecture prompted employees to withdraw socially and interact over email and instant messaging instead.
claims.episode_span: while electronic messaging and email volume rose to fill the gap
claims.supporting_quote: Open-plan office designs (e.g., tables with no visual barriers) reduce short-term building costs, compared to cubicles or private offices, but result in persistently lower productivity , dramatically fewer face-to-face interactions among staff, and a higher number of sick days .

claims.claim: The Quickborner consulting group was established in 1958 by brothers Wolfgang and Eberhard Schnelle in Germany, and developed the office-landscape (Bürolandschaft) concept.
claims.episode_span: The modern open-plan movement traces its roots to the Quickborner Team, a German management consultancy that developed the Bürolandschaft concept in 1958
claims.supporting_quote: In 1958, the Quickborner consulting group was established by two brothers, Wolfgang and Eberhard Schnelle, who had previously been working as assistants in their father’s furniture studio.

claims.claim: Office landscape aimed to seat all levels of staff together on one open floor to create a non-hierarchical environment that increased communication and collaboration.
claims.episode_span: Quickborner designers argued that rigid walls and fixed desks reinforced hierarchy and blocked the informal exchanges needed for complex problem-solving in postwar industry
claims.supporting_quote: Office landscape encouraged all levels of staff to sit together in one open floor to create a non-hierarchical environment that increased communication and collaboration.

claims.claim: Robert Propst, head of research at furniture maker Herman Miller (hired 1958), was an early advocate of Bürolandschaft in America.
claims.episode_span: By the late 1960s the Bürolandschaft model had crossed the Atlantic, promoted by furniture manufacturers such as Herman Miller
claims.supporting_quote: An early advocate for Bürolandschaft in America was Robert Propst , who was hired as the head of the research wing of the furniture company Herman Miller 1958.
